speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe the nature of your headache and specify if the vision loss is in one eye or both?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your age and symptoms, I need to check for signs of inflammation; do you experience any pain or tenderness when chewing or brushing your hair, and have you noticed any jaw claudication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned having no other pain, but specifically, do you experience any scalp tenderness or pain in your jaw when chewing? I also need to know if you have noticed any double vision or if the vision loss is accompanied by drooping of the eyelid.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the history. I need to assess for temporal artery tenderness and check your visual fields directly. REQUEST TEST: ESR
REQUEST TEST: CRP

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal inflammatory markers make giant cell arteritis less likely. I need to rule out other causes such as increased intracranial pressure or a structural lesion; do you experience nausea, vomiting, or pulsatile tinnitus, and have you noticed any new neurological deficits like weakness or speech difficulties? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI results effectively rule out most structural causes like tumors or strokes. Given the progressive nature of the vision loss and headache in an older adult, I need to consider compressive lesions of the optic nerve or chiasm that might not be fully characterized yet; REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Since structural and inflammatory causes have been largely ruled out, I need to assess your ocular pressure; have you experienced any halos around lights or eye pain, and when did you last have a comprehensive eye exam including visual field testing? REQUEST TEST: Visual_Field_Test

speaker: Doctor
text:
Normal visual fields help rule out glaucoma and some compressive lesions. To distinguish between optic nerve and retinal causes, I need to know if you have noticed any blind spots (scotomas) or if the vision loss is central (affecting detailed vision) versus peripheral.

REQUEST TEST: OCT_Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal OCT, MRI, ESR, CRP, and visual fields, we must look toward functional or metabolic causes given the negative structural workup. Do you have a history of diabetes or thyroid disease, and have you noticed any changes in your color vision?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the progressive vision loss and headache in an elderly patient with a completely negative workup for structural, inflammatory, and common ocular causes, I must consider functional or non-organic etiologies. DIAGNOSIS READY: Psychogenic visual loss
